item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 222328
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Tue Sep 22 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Major
Hurricane Polo, located less than 200 miles offshore of southern
Mexico, and on Tropical Storm Odalys, located well west-southwest of
the southern tip of Baja California.

Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands (Former TD 15-E):
Showers and thunderstorms associated with the remnants of Tropical
Depression Fifteen-E, located roughly 430 miles south-southeast of
South Point, Hawaii, are gradually becoming better organized.
Environmental conditions are conducive for development, and a
tropical depression is expected to form in a day or so, while the
system moves slowly west-northwestward. Heavy rains associated with
this system are forecast to spread over the southeastern Hawaiian
Islands starting on Wednesday and continuing through Saturday,
possibly resulting in life-threatening flash flooding and mudslides
for portions of the Big Island and Maui. Interests in the Hawaiian
Islands should continue to monitor the progress of this system.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

South of the Gulf of Tehuantepec:
An area of low pressure is expected to form in a couple of days to
the south of the Gulf of Tehuantepec. Afterwards, environmental
conditions should be favorable for gradual development, and a
tropical depression is likely to form late this week or this weekend
as the system moves slowly west-northwestward to northwestward,
parallel to the coast of southern and southwestern Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

$$
Forecaster Hagen

----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.1N 130.1W
ABOUT 1425 MI...2290 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA

PRESENT MOVEMENT...ENE OR 60 DEGREES AT 3 MPH...6 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...994 MB...29.36 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Odalys was
located near latitude 15.1 North, longitude 130.1 West. Odalys is
moving toward the east-northeast near 3 mph (6 km/h) and this 
motion is expected to continue through the next couple of days, 
followed by a gradual turn to the northeast late this week.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 70 mph (110 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Additional strengthening is forecast, and Odalys
could become a hurricane later today or tonight.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 160 miles (260 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 994 mb (29.36 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM PDT.

item.title: Tropical Storm Odalys Forecast Discussion Number 11
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Tue Sep 22 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 222043
TCDEP1
 
Tropical Storm Odalys Discussion Number  11
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP162026
200 PM PDT Tue Sep 22 2026

Deep convection was on a positive trend until recently, when the 
cloud tops started to warm based on the data from infrared satellite 
imagery, likely due to entering the diurnal convective minimum. The 
latest subjective TAFB Dvorak fix was T3.5/55 kt, which is the same 
as the last several cycles. The objective satellite intensity 
estimates from UW-CIMSS are in the range of 53-70 kt. Therefore, the 
initial intensity has been raised to 60 kt for this advisory.

The cyclone is currently moving east-northeastward, or 60/3 kt. This 
general motion is expected to persist as a trough that is moving 
over the eastern Pacific toward the western coast of the United 
States should deepen further. After this, the trough will become the 
main steering flow for Odalys resulting in an east-northeastward or 
northeastward motion for the next few days. After 72 h, the 
uncertainty in the track increases as potential interaction with 
Hurricane Polo could cause Odalys to slow down later in the forecast 
period. The current NHC track forecast is similar to the previous 
track with only a few minor adjustments and continues to be in good 
agreement with the HCCA and GDMI forecast aids.  

The cyclone is forecasted to be in an environment with weaker wind 
shear, plenty of mid-level moisture, and warm sea-surface 
temperatures, and this is expected to lead to additional 
intensification over the next few days. Thus, Odalys is forecast to 
become a hurricane tonight. After 48 h, Odalys will encounter a 
drier mid-level air mass and increased upper-level outflow from 
Hurricane Polo. The current NHC intensity guidance remains on the 
upper end of the model guidance, but close to the HCCA and GDMI 
forecast aids.

item.description:

BULLETIN
Hurricane Polo Intermediate Advisory Number 9A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
600 PM CST Tue Sep 22 2026
 
...POLO DRIFTING SLOWLY AS IT REMAINS AN EXTREMELY DANGEROUS 
CATEGORY 5 HURRICANE...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 600 PM CST...0000 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...14.6N 101.4W
ABOUT 215 MI...345 KM S OF ZIHUATANEJO MEXICO
ABOUT 360 MI...580 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...175 MPH...280 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...E OR 90 DEGREES AT 1 MPH...2 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...900 MB...26.58 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* Tecpan de Galeana to Punta San Telmo
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* West of Punta San Telmo to Playa Perula
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area within 36 hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Interests elsewhere along the southwestern Mexico coast should
continue to monitor the progress of this system as additional
watches and warnings could be necessary tonight.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 600 PM CST (0000 UTC), the center of Hurricane Polo was located 
near latitude 14.6 North, longitude 101.4 West. Polo is drifting 
toward the east near 1 mph (2 km/h). A slow northwestward motion is 
expected to begin tonight followed by a general west-northwestward 
motion over the next few days. On the forecast track, the core of 
Polo is expected to be near the coast of southwestern Mexico through 
the middle of this week, although it is forecast to remain offshore.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 175 mph (280 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Polo is a category 5 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson 
Hurricane Wind Scale. Fluctuations in intensity are expected over 
the next few days, though Polo is expected to remain a very powerful 
major hurricane. 
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 90
miles (150 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 900 mb (26.58 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Polo can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP2 and WMO header WTPZ42 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are expected within the warning
area along the coast of Mexico by early Wednesday.  Tropical storm
conditions are possible within the watch area along the coast of
Mexico by Thursday.
 
RAINFALL: Polo is expected to produce rainfall totals of 3 to 6
inches, with isolated maximum totals up to 8 inches across coastal
portions of the Mexican states of Guerrero and Michoacán through
Thursday. This rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and
mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain. Rainfall of 2 to 4
inches is possible in coastal portions of Oaxaca, Colima, and
Jalisco through Thursday.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Polo,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURF:  Swells generated by Polo are expected to affect portions of
the coast of southwestern Mexico during the next few days. These
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf, rip current
conditions, and coastal flooding. Please consult products from
your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Papin

item.title: Hurricane Polo Forecast Discussion Number 9
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Tue Sep 22 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 222047
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Polo Discussion Number   9
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
300 PM CST Tue Sep 22 2026
 
A NOAA Hurricane Hunter aircraft investigated Hurricane Polo this
afternoon and found that it had strengthened even more since this
morning.  The highest 700 mb flight-level winds were 168 kt, which
corresponds to 151 kt at the surface using a standard reduction
factor.  However, the aircraft also found that the central pressure
had dropped to an extremely low value of about 892 mb. This would
typically support even higher winds than 151 kt, so the advisory
intensity is set conservatively to 155 kt.  The system continues to
look very impressive on satellite imagery with very deep convection
and well-defined upper-level outflow.  The radial profile of the
aircraft wind data show hints of a secondary wind maximum so a
concentric eyewall may be developing.
 
Aircraft and satellite center fixes indicate little movement over
the past few hours.  Global models show a mid-tropospheric ridge
becoming established over Mexico during the next couple of days.
This evolution of the steering pattern should result in a
west-northwestward track in the 48- to 72-hour time frame.  In 4-5
days, the steering currents are more uncertain.  However, Polo
appears likely to slow down and turn more northward by that time.
The official forecast is very similar to the previous NHC track.
 
Polo should remain in a very conducive environment of low vertical 
wind shear, extremely warm ocean waters, and a very moist low- to 
mid-level air mass for the next several days.  Therefore even more 
strengthening is possible.  Given the suggestion of concentric 
eyewall formation however, only a slight increase in intensity is 
forecast tonight and fluctuations in intensity are likely over the 
next few days.  However, the hurricane is expected to remain very 
intense through this week and, in fact, maintain category 5 strength 
for a couple of days.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Heavy rainfall associated with Polo will impact coastal portions
of southwest Mexico through Thursday.  This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
2. A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for portions of
southwestern Mexico, and the Tropical Storm Watch is in effect 
westward to Playa Perula. Interests in these areas should closely
monitor updates to the forecast.

CORRECTED PRESSURE IN INCHES

...HURRICANE HUNTER AIRCRAFT FINDS POLO HAS STRENGTHENED EVEN 
MORE...
 
Reports from a NOAA Hurricane Hunter aircraft indicate that the 
maximum winds in Hurricane Polo have increased to near 180 mph 
(285 km/h) with higher gusts.  The minimum central pressure has 
dropped to 892 mb...26.34 inches.

Polo is nearly stationary but is expected to move generally 
west-northwestward over the next couple of days.
